questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to study in a French speaking country, and at a reputable university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My opinion, would vary based on what people see as important, and what they are already used to.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not easy. I was using emails I had recieved in July to find out what to do.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were poeple on campus to help with questions. We recieved an email about orientation. Asking questions via email in the first 2 weeks wasn't the best, as they didn't reply very fast. There was a big Erasmus orientation, but the session was all in French (alright for me, but maybe not for others).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Sorbonne has an agreement with Cite Internationale Universitaire de Paris, so I found accomodation at the Dutch College. If you're Danish, you probably stay at the Danish College.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is very sociable, a dorm, so be ready for that.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would have prefered a studio, but there weren't any available.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Initially registration for courses was done via email in June before the exchange. This was alright, though scant information available about each course. When I arrived, I wanted to change my courses, which was very difficult, because the Sorbonne exchange coordinator for my department made us all construct and schedule our own timetables.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You have contact with the overall exchange/mobility office, who you can email, and your department coordinator. Mostly by email, but also by going to the office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I didn't get all the courses I wanted. I wasn't sure what I wanted becuase there wasn't much information on what was there. Not many classes are available in English, so be prepared to study in French.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Write down the contact details, including email, office and title for each of the contact people. Be prepared to go to the office during office hours to speed up the process. Don't expect fast email responses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was difficult, and perhaps someone with a proper computer science background might find the courses more manageable. Long weeks, 30 hours a week for 30 ECTS course load.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took M1, master 1 courses. They were very maths heavy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very much individual focused, not much teamwork or group work. Very dictatorial, not a lot of time to ask questions. Very few breaks between and during classes. Usually, 2 hours for a tutorial or lecture, with no break, and then only 15 minutes between each 2 hour block.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: MLBDA, LRC, MAPSI, COMPLEX (All in French), COMNET (In English).

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: COMNET. It was in English, and probably the easiest. Same for MLBDA, but is in French.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Meat at supermarkets, and just supermarkets are quite expensive. Beer at some bars is very expensive, range is: 26 DKK - 105 DKK for a beer.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not at the university, but at the residence, where there are many sports and clubs available.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: At the Cite Internationale there are sports like tennis, badminton, a gym, etc. There are also sports that take place on the grounds that are free to join.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Get involved in your residence/houses' social activities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Fontainbleau, not far from Paris, and a way to connect with nature.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Living with other exchange students made it easier. Expect to speak French outside when you interact with people.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talking to French students is challenging, but it helps if your French is good. Will most likely befriend other exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The (Parisian) french can be quite cold. Don't take it personally. Some of them are nice.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their willingness to speak French with you.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Make sure you have good French. Make sure you know what courses you will do, and if you are capable of succeeding with them (Sorbonne is very intense, even for French students, and is known for a high level of maths).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Days can be long, and exam periods stressful. Go away and do something fun sometimes.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from around the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The courses.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
